Symptom: PC1 on Fa0/5 cannot reach the file server in VLAN 30. It gets an IP but no connectivity to anything.
Topology_Notes: L2 switch SW1 with VLAN 10 (clients) and VLAN 30 (servers). Fa0/5 should be an access port in VLAN 30.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show vlan brief", "output": "VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/5, Fa0/6, Fa0/7, Fa0/8
10   Clients                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
30   Servers                          active    Fa0/10"}, {"command": "show interfaces Fa0/5 switchport", "output": "Name: Fa0/5
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)"}]
Expected_Fault: Fa0/5 is still assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30.

Symptom: Devices in VLAN 20 on SW2 cannot reach VLAN 20 devices on SW1 across the trunk link, but VLAN 10 works fine.
Topology_Notes: SW1 and SW2 connected via Gi0/1 trunk. VLANs 10, 20, 30 exist on both switches.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show interfaces trunk", "output": "Port      Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1     on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port      Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1     1,10,30"}]
Expected_Fault: VLAN 20 is not included in the trunk allowed VLAN list.

Symptom: New PCs joining VLAN 10 fail to receive an IP address; existing PCs still work.
Topology_Notes: Router-on-a-stick providing DHCP for VLAN 10 (192.168.10.0/26 - only 64 addresses).
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show ip dhcp pool", "output": "Pool VLAN10_POOL :
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Subnet size (first/last)       : 0 / 0
 Total addresses                : 62
 Leased addresses               : 62
 Pending event                  : none"}]
Expected_Fault: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 has 62 usable addresses, all leased - pool exhaustion.

Symptom: PCs can ping 8.8.8.8 by IP but "ping www.cisco.pt" fails with "Ping request could not find host".
Topology_Notes: Clients use DHCP-assigned DNS server 10.0.0.53 hosted on a separate VLAN reachable through the core router.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "ipconfig /all", "output": "IP Address......: 10.0.10.25
Subnet Mask......: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway..: 10.0.10.1
DNS Servers......: 10.0.0.53"}, {"command": "show ip route", "output": "10.0.10.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan10
10.0.0.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan99"}]
Expected_Fault: DNS server IP is configured, but no route/ACL issue was visible; ICMP to raw IP works so L3 path exists - likely DNS service down or ACL blocking UDP/53 specifically.

Symptom: Internal LAN devices can reach each other and internal servers, but nothing outside the local network (e.g. no Internet access).
Topology_Notes: Edge router R1 connects internal LAN to ISP via Se0/0/0. Internal routing between VLANs works fine.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show ip route", "output": "C    192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0\nC    192.168.2.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1\nC    203.0.113.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0"}]
Expected_Fault: No default route (0.0.0.0/0) exists pointing to the ISP - no gateway of last resort configured.

Symptom: Branch office (192.168.30.0/24) cannot reach HQ subnet (192.168.10.0/24); traceroute stops after the branch router.
Topology_Notes: Branch router R2 has a static route to HQ. WAN link between R2 and R1 is 172.16.0.0/30.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show ip route", "output": "S    192.168.10.0/24 [1/0] via 172.16.0.6\nC    172.16.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0"}, {"command": "show interfaces Serial0/0/0", "output": "Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up\n  Internet address is 172.16.0.5/30"}]
Expected_Fault: Static route next hop 172.16.0.6 is outside the /30 WAN subnet (172.16.0.4-172.16.0.7 usable is only .5 and .6, but .6 should be the R1 side - verify actual R1 IP; if R1 is .5 itself this is a self-referential/wrong next hop).

Symptom: Network admin cannot Telnet into R1 (192.168.1.1) from the management VLAN, connection times out.
Topology_Notes: R1 has VTY lines protected by an access-class ACL restricting management access.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show access-lists", "output": "Standard IP access list MGMT_ACL
    10 permit 192.168.99.10
    20 deny any (5 matches)"}, {"command": "show run | section line vty", "output": "line vty 0 4
 access-class MGMT_ACL in
 login local"}]
Expected_Fault: MGMT_ACL only permits a single host (192.168.99.10); the admin's actual source IP is being denied by the implicit/explicit deny.

Symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the Internet despite having correct default routes; "show ip nat translations" is empty.
Topology_Notes: R1 performs PAT (NAT overload) from inside VLAN 10 to the ISP-facing interface.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show run | include ip nat", "output": "interface GigabitEthernet0/0\n ip nat inside\nip nat inside source list NAT_ACL interface Serial0/0/0 overload"}, {"command": "show ip nat translations", "output": "Total translations: 0 (0 static, 0 dynamic; 0 extended)"}]
Expected_Fault: Serial0/0/0 (the outside/ISP-facing interface) is missing "ip nat outside", so NAT never triggers.

Symptom: PCs in newly added VLAN 40 (192.168.40.0/24) cannot access the Internet; VLAN 10 and 20 work fine.
Topology_Notes: PAT configured with NAT_ACL matching only the original two subnets.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show access-lists NAT_ACL", "output": "Standard IP access list NAT_ACL\n    10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255\n    20 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255"}]
Expected_Fault: NAT_ACL does not include 192.168.40.0/24, so traffic from VLAN 40 is never translated.

Symptom: Inter-switch link between SW1 and SW2 carries only VLAN 1 traffic; other VLANs across the link fail entirely.
Topology_Notes: Gi0/1 on SW1 and SW2 should form an 802.1q trunk.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show interfaces trunk (SW1)", "output": "Port      Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1     on           802.1q         trunking      1"}, {"command": "show interfaces switchport (SW2 Gi0/1)", "output": "Name: Gi0/1
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access"}]
Expected_Fault: SW2 Gi0/1 is configured as a static access port, not trunk, causing a mode mismatch with SW1.

Symptom: Intermittent connectivity issues and CDP native VLAN mismatch messages appear in the switch log between SW1 and SW3.
Topology_Notes: Trunk link Gi0/2 connects SW1 and SW3.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show interfaces trunk (SW1)", "output": "Port      Mode   Encapsulation  Status     Native vlan\nGi0/2     on     802.1q         trunking   1"}, {"command": "show interfaces trunk (SW3)", "output": "Port      Mode   Encapsulation  Status     Native vlan\nGi0/2     on     802.1q         trunking   99"}]
Expected_Fault: Native VLAN differs between the two ends of the trunk (VLAN 1 vs VLAN 99).

Symptom: Two PCs on VLAN 10 have intermittent connectivity; both occasionally lose network access when the other is active.
Topology_Notes: Static IPs assigned manually to lab PCs; DHCP not used on this VLAN by design.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show ip arp", "output": "Internet  10.0.10.15   -   0060.2F3A.1B2C  ARPA  Vlan10\nInternet  10.0.10.15   -   0060.2F9C.44D1  ARPA  Vlan10"}]
Expected_Fault: Two different MAC addresses map to the same IP 10.0.10.15 - duplicate static IP assignment.

Symptom: PC on VLAN 10 cannot ping its own default gateway despite correct-looking IP and gateway values.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "ipconfig", "output": "IP Address......: 192.168.10.55\nSubnet Mask......: 255.255.255.192\nDefault Gateway..: 192.168.10.1"}]
Expected_Fault: Subnet mask 255.255.255.192 (/26) puts the gateway 192.168.10.1 in a different subnet block than host .55 - verify subnet boundaries.

Symptom: All PCs in VLAN 20 lost Internet and inter-VLAN access after a network re-addressing change.
Topology_Notes: VLAN 20 SVI was renumbered from 192.168.20.1/24 to 192.168.21.1/24; PCs use static gateways.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "ipconfig", "output": "IP Address......: 192.168.20.40
Subnet Mask......: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway..: 192.168.20.1"}, {"command": "show running-config interface Vlan20", "output": "interface Vlan20
 ip address 192.168.21.1 255.255.255.0"}]
Expected_Fault: PC still references the old gateway 192.168.20.1, but the SVI is now 192.168.21.1 on a different subnet.

Symptom: Laptop repeatedly prompts for the Wi-Fi password and never connects to "LAB-WIFI".
Topology_Notes: Wireless router configured with WPA2-PSK on SSID LAB-WIFI.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show running-config (wireless router)", "output": "ssid LAB-WIFI\n authentication open\n wpa-psk ascii 0 CorrectHorseBattery"}]
Expected_Fault: Authentication is set to "open" while a WPA-PSK key is also configured - conflicting security mode causes client handshake failures.

Symptom: Users report they cannot find "LAB-WIFI" in their available networks list, though wired clients see the AP is up.
Topology_Notes: SSID broadcast toggled off during a prior lab.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show running-config (wireless router)", "output": "ssid LAB-WIFI\n broadcast-ssid disable"}]
Expected_Fault: SSID broadcast is disabled, hiding the network from client scan lists.

Symptom: Branch office is completely unreachable from HQ; link light on the WAN interface at the branch appears off.
Topology_Notes: R2 Serial0/0/1 connects branch to HQ via a leased line.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show ip interface brief", "output": "Serial0/0/1            172.16.1.2      YES manual administratively down down"}]
Expected_Fault: Serial0/0/1 is administratively down - someone issued a "shutdown" command.

Symptom: File transfers to the server on Fa0/10 are extremely slow and the switch log shows many CRC/late-collision errors.
Topology_Notes: Server NIC manually set to full-duplex; switch port set to auto.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show interfaces Fa0/10", "output": "Fa0/10 is up, line protocol is up\n  Full-duplex, 100Mb/s\n  1532 input errors, 985 CRC, 640 late collisions"}]
Expected_Fault: High late-collision/CRC counts alongside full-duplex on the switch side suggest a duplex mismatch with the server NIC (half vs full).

Symptom: Newly created VLAN 50 devices cannot reach any other VLAN, though VLAN 50 itself works for local L2 traffic.
Topology_Notes: Router-on-a-stick R1 with Gi0/0 trunked to SW1, subinterfaces for VLAN 10/20/30 exist.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show running-config | include interface Gi", "output": "interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 encapsulation dot1Q 10
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 30"}]
Expected_Fault: No Gi0/0.50 subinterface exists for VLAN 50, so the router cannot route for that VLAN.

Symptom: R1 and R2 form an OSPF adjacency that never progresses past EXSTART; routes are not being learned.
Topology_Notes: R1 and R2 run OSPF area 0 over a point-to-point link; R2 interface has a non-default MTU.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show ip ospf neighbor", "output": "Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface\n2.2.2.2           1   EXSTART/  -      00:00:35    172.16.0.2      Serial0/0/0"}, {"command": "show interfaces Serial0/0/0 (R1)", "output": "MTU 1500 bytes"}, {"command": "show interfaces Serial0/0/0 (R2)", "output": "MTU 1400 bytes"}]
Expected_Fault: MTU mismatch (1500 on R1 vs 1400 on R2) prevents OSPF database exchange from completing, stalling adjacency in EXSTART.

Symptom: Internal users can no longer reach the web server even though the ACL was meant to only restrict inbound Internet traffic.
Topology_Notes: ACL 101 applied on Gi0/0 (LAN-facing) instead of Se0/0/0 (WAN-facing).
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show run | include access-group", "output": "interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip access-group 101 in"}, {"command": "show access-lists 101", "output": "Extended IP access list 101
    10 deny tcp any any eq 80
    20 permit ip any any"}]
Expected_Fault: ACL 101 is applied inbound on the LAN interface Gi0/0, blocking internal users' outbound HTTP requests instead.

Symptom: Attempt to block only Telnet (TCP/23) to R2 from a specific subnet instead blocks all traffic from that subnet.
Topology_Notes: Standard ACL matches source address only and cannot filter by port/protocol.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show access-lists", "output": "Standard IP access list 10\n    10 deny 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255\n    20 permit any"}]
Expected_Fault: A standard ACL matches source address only and cannot filter by port/protocol, so it denies ALL traffic from 192.168.50.0/24.

Symptom: PC on Fa0/8 suddenly lost network connectivity after an unauthorized laptop was plugged in.
Topology_Notes: Fa0/8 has port security with maximum 1 MAC, violation mode shutdown.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show port-security interface Fa0/8", "output": "Port Security: Enabled
Port Status: Secure-shutdown
Violation Mode: Shutdown
Maximum MAC Addresses: 1
SecurityViolation Count: 1"}]
Expected_Fault: Port security detected a second MAC address on Fa0/8 and placed it into err-disabled state.

Symptom: SW3 has two uplinks but one is blocked by STP. Traffic fails when the active link's transceiver is bad.
Topology_Notes: SW3 uplinks Gi0/1 and Gi0/2 to two core switches; STP root port is down but alternate hasn't transitioned.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show spanning-tree", "output": "Interface           Role Sts Cost      Prio.Nbr Type\nGi0/1               Root FWD 4         128.1    P2p\nGi0/2               Altn BLK 4         128.2    P2p"}, {"command": "show interfaces Gi0/1", "output": "GigabitEthernet0/1 is down, line protocol is down (notconnect)"}]
Expected_Fault: STP root port Gi0/1 is physically down, and alternate Gi0/2 has not transitioned to forwarding.

Symptom: PC gets IP but cannot reach server in VLAN 30; gateway ping works.
Topology_Notes: L3 switch with VLAN 10 (clients) and VLAN 30 (servers), SVIs configured for inter-VLAN routing.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show ip route", "output": "10.0.10.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan10
10.0.30.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan30"}, {"command": "show access-lists", "output": "Extended IP access list BLOCK_SERVERS
    10 deny ip 10.0.10.0 0.0.0.255 10.0.30.0 0.0.0.255
    20 permit ip any any"}]
Expected_Fault: ACL BLOCK_SERVERS explicitly denies client-to-server traffic before the permit any any.

Symptom: PCs on VLAN 40 never receive an IP lease; VLAN 10 (with DHCP server) works fine.
Topology_Notes: Central DHCP server lives on VLAN 10; VLAN 40 is routed separately.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show running-config interface Vlan40", "output": "interface Vlan40\n ip address 192.168.40.1 255.255.255.0\n! no ip helper-address configured"}]
Expected_Fault: No "ip helper-address" is configured on the VLAN 40 SVI, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the server.

Symptom: Only the first two PCs in VLAN 10 receive IP addresses via DHCP; others fail.
Topology_Notes: DHCP pool for 192.168.10.0/24 configured with excluded-address range.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show running-config | section dhcp", "output": "ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.253
ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.10.1"}]
Expected_Fault: The excluded range (192.168.10.1 - 192.168.10.253) removes nearly the entire pool, leaving only .254.

Symptom: Internal DNS resolves local hosts but external lookups (e.g. google.com) time out.
Topology_Notes: Internal DNS server configured to forward unresolved queries to public DNS.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show running-config (DNS server)", "output": "dns forwarder 198.51.100.99\nip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1"}, {"command": "ping 198.51.100.99", "output": "Request timed out. Success rate is 0 percent (0/4)"}]
Expected_Fault: The configured upstream DNS forwarder 198.51.100.99 is unreachable.

Symptom: PCs using virtual gateway IP intermittently lose gateway connectivity.
Topology_Notes: R1 and R2 run HSRP for VLAN 10 with virtual IP 192.168.10.1.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show standby brief (R1)", "output": "Interface  Grp  Pri P State    Active       Standby      Virtual IP\nVl10       10   100   Standby  unknown      local        192.168.10.1"}, {"command": "show standby brief (R2)", "output": "Interface  Grp  Pri P State    Active       Standby      Virtual IP\nVl10       10   100   Standby  unknown      local        192.168.10.1"}]
Expected_Fault: Both HSRP routers report themselves as Standby with Active unknown - multicast hellos are blocked.

Symptom: One specific laptop cannot join SSID while all other devices connect successfully.
Topology_Notes: AP requires WPA2-PSK (AES) but laptop profile was created with WPA-TKIP.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show wireless client profile (laptop)", "output": "SSID: LAB-WIFI\nSecurity: WPA-PSK (TKIP)\nAP requires: WPA2-PSK (AES)"}]
Expected_Fault: The laptop's profile uses outdated WPA-TKIP while the AP only accepts WPA2-PSK/AES.

Symptom: A single lab PC shows untagged VLAN warnings and cannot get a DHCP lease.
Topology_Notes: Fa0/12 should be a simple access port in VLAN 10.
Show_Commands_Output:
[{"command": "show interfaces Fa0/12 switchport", "output": "Name: Fa0/12
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: trunk
Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1 (default)"}]
Expected_Fault: Fa0/12 was configured as a trunk port instead of access.

Symptom: Internal users can initiate sessions but return traffic is dropped; sessions hang.
Topology_Notes: Inbound ACL on WAN interface intended to allow return traffic for internal sessions.
Show_Commands_Output: [{"command": "show access-lists 120", "output": "Extended IP access list 120\n    10 permit tcp any any eq 80\n    20 deny ip any any"}]
Expected_Fault: The inbound WAN ACL lacks the "established" keyword, blocking incoming TCP response packets.
